call_goal: Learn whether Pellucid Travel has a real problem with its trip-planning agent, why now, and who else cares
desired_outcomes: Their top problems in their words

transcript.text: What prompted you to take this call now?
Mostly planning season. We're scoping next year, and the trip-planning agent is the thing everyone's asking about.
How does the agent work today, end to end?
A traveller asks for a trip, the agent searches flights and hotels through our booking APIs, builds an itinerary, and a human approves anything over a certain value.
Where does it go wrong, when it does?
The biggest problem is it sometimes recommends hotels that are already sold out. The availability data it reads is stale.
How do you find out when that happens?
Customer complaints, mostly. Or the human approver catches it before it goes out.
How often does the approver catch it?
Maybe a few times a week? We don't really track it anywhere.
Who looks at those cases today?
Me and one other engineer. We pull the conversation logs and read through them.
What happens after you've read them?
We tweak the prompt and ship it. And honestly that's the second problem: when something gets worse, we can't tell which prompt version caused it.
How many prompt versions are live at once?
Usually two or three, we split traffic between them.
How do you decide which version wins?
Right now there's a spreadsheet of about two hundred test trips that Lucia's team runs by hand. That's the third thing: it takes a full day and only one person really knows how it works.
Who else uses the results of that spreadsheet?
Product looks at it before a release, and I sign off on it.
How often do you release a new version?
Every two weeks, roughly, sometimes faster if something's off.
Which booking APIs does the agent call?
Two flight providers and our own hotel inventory service. The hotel one is the stale one.
What model are you running underneath it?
A mix: a big model for planning and a small one for the search calls.
Where do the conversation logs live today?
In our data warehouse, we export them every night.
Is anyone else evaluating tools for this?
Not formally. We looked at a couple of things last year but didn't pick anything.
How big is the team working on the agent?
Six people, plus Lucia's two engineers part time.

unacceptable_behaviors: Asks another new discovery question instead of playing back (16 questions since any play-back)
Plays back something they didn't say, or adds pain they didn't name
acceptable_questions: So: sold-out hotels, unclear prompt versions, a hand-run test sheet. Did I miss anything?
Let me play that back: stale hotel data, which prompt changed, the spreadsheet. Fair?
